Knowledge Assistant and Supervisor Agent are now legacy offerings. For new agents written in code, Databricks recommends the Agent Bricks CLI. To build agents without code, use Genie Agents. See Legacy agent offerings.

## Feature Views are now generally available​

October 12, 2026

Feature Views are now generally available for batch, streaming, and request-time data. They will be enabled for compliance security profile workspaces in mid-November 2026. See Feature Views. [...] See Transactions.

## Data Classification API is now generally available​

October 14, 2026

The Data Classification API and its Terraform resource are now generally available. Auto-tagging configuration (`auto_tag_configs`) remains in Public Preview. See the API reference.

## Workspace-level package repositories for Databricks Apps are generally available​

October 14, 2026 [...] October 6, 2026

DeepSeek V4 Flash (0731) will be retired on November 5, 2026. DeepSeek V4.1 Flash is the recommended replacement. See Deprecated and retired models for migration guidance.

## Use multiple triggers for Lakeflow Jobs (Beta)​")

October 5, 2026

Lakeflow Jobs can now use up to five triggers. You can combine trigger types, add multiple triggers of the same type, and pause each trigger independently. See Add multiple triggers to a job.

| Headline launches | Genie One (GA), Genie Ontology, Agent Bricks, Unity Catalog Metrics, Unity AI Gateway, LTAP, Lakehouse RT | [...] Read together, the Summit announcements describe one strategy: build a stack where agents are first-class, governed at runtime, and grounded in business meaning. Three themes connect every group. First, agentic AI is moving from lab to enterprise, which is why Genie One went GA and Agent Bricks opened to more frameworks. Second, AI cost is now an executive concern, which is why Unity AI Gateway leads with spend caps and smart routing and why LTAP and Lakehouse RT collapse redundant [...] | LTAP | Lake Transactional/Analytical Processing; unifies OLTP and OLAP on one copy | Coming soon (Lakebase) |

results.title: DAIS 2026: The Databricks Announcements I Think Cl... - Databricks Community - 159914
results.content:
I also paid attention to the security and compliance announcements: Automatic Identity Management for Entra ID, Okta support in preview, Context-Based Ingress, Private Network Gateway, Lakebase private connectivity, HITRUST across clouds, expanded GovCloud support, and FedRAMP High support coming on Azure Commercial.

This is the work that makes AI usable in regulated environments. It may not get the loudest applause, but clients will care about it when they move from pilots to production. [...] This is why I found this year’s announcements interesting. They were not only about adding more capability. They were about reducing the distance between data, context, AI, governance, and action.

### Context is becoming the real AI foundation

The announcement around Genie One, Genie Agents, and Genie Ontology was one of the strongest signals from the summit. [...] Marketplace and OpenSharing extend this to partners and data providers.

The Marketplace commit drawdown and upcoming transactability are important for commercial adoption. Partners can reach Databricks customers more directly and shorten sales cycles by using pre-committed spend. Apps and Genie Agents can also be distributed through Marketplace, which opens new packaging models.

The most important thing I took away from Data + AI Summit 2026 was not one product announcement.
It was the direction.
Databricks is building around a very real enterprise problem: companies want AI to help with decisions, operations, customer engagement, software development, security, and analytics, but the AI has to work inside the reality of the business.

Source: https://community.databricks.com/t5/community-articles/dais-2026-the-databricks-announcements-i-think-clients-should/td-p/159914
Title: DAIS 2026: The Databricks Announcements I Think Cl... - Databricks Community - 159914
Content: That reality includes messy data, strict permissions, different definitions of the same metric, pipelines that break, models that drift, sensitive customer data, many clouds, many tools, and teams that already have enough platforms to manage.
This is why I found this year’s announcements interesting. They were not only about adding more capability. They were about reducing the distance between data, context, AI, governance, and action.
Context is becoming the real AI foundation
The announcement around Genie One, Genie Agents, and Genie Ontology was one of the strongest signals from the summit.
The reason is simple. A business user does not need another generic chatbot. They need an AI experience that understands how their company works.

Content: The managed Omnigent direction on Databricks is especially practical: shared history, remote access, collaboration, isolated execution, and governance through Unity AI Gateway.
My view is that agent development is about to look more like software engineering and platform engineering. The teams that treat agents only as prompts will struggle. The teams that treat agents as governed systems will move faster and with less risk.
ZeroOps is one of the most practical announcements
I liked Genie ZeroOps because it is close to the daily pain of data and ML teams.
Anyone who has worked on a production data platform knows this pattern. A pipeline fails. A schema changes. A table looks fine but the data quality has silently changed. A dashboard number moves and nobody immediately knows whether it is a real business change or a data issue. A model starts producing weaker predictions without throwing an error.

Content: Real-time is moving closer to the lakehouse
Lakehouse//RT, Lakebase, Lakeflow, and LTAP all connect to a long-running architecture issue.
Many companies still use separate systems for transactions, analytics, streaming, serving, applications, and AI. This creates copies of data, sync jobs, governance gaps, and additional places where things can fail.
Lakehouse//RT is Databricks’ answer for real-time operational analytics, BI, app serving, and observability workloads directly on the lakehouse. The message I liked from the Lakehouse//RT announcement is that separate serving layers have a real cost: duplication, governance drift, and engineering overhead."

# Executive Pre-Meeting Briefing: Databricks Strategic Update

## Overview
This briefing document has been prepared for the upcoming stakeholder meeting on November 20, 2026. It provides a concise, high-impact review of Databricks' recent corporate, product, and ecosystem developments over the preceding 30 days (mid-October to mid-November 2026). The scope encompasses critical platform releases, integration capabilities, and enterprise-grade generative AI governance frameworks designed to streamline data operations.

## Recent Developments

Databricks has accelerated its platform evolution, emphasizing deep integration between generative AI agents, data governance, and automated operational pipelines. Based on recent official release notes and platform announcements, the most significant updates focus on the expansion of the Genie ecosystem, Lakeflow pipeline automation, and advanced developer tool integrations ([Databricks Release Notes - November 2026 Latest Updates - Releasebot](https://releasebot.io/updates/databricks)).

### Generative AI and Genie Ecosystem Enhancements
The expansion of the Genie ecosystem represents a major architectural push to embed context-aware AI directly into developer and enterprise workflows. 
* **Genie One Desktop & Chrome Integration:** The Genie One desktop application is now generally available on macOS, accompanied by a Beta Chrome extension that replaces the standard new tab page with the Genie One workspace interface ([Databricks Release Notes - November 2026 Latest Updates - Releasebot](https://releasebot.io/updates/databricks)). This tool allows users to execute queries and search connected tools seamlessly using existing credentials.
* **Developer Tool Interoperability:** Unity Gateway now supports connecting GitHub Copilot CLI and Visual Studio Code environments with Claude, GPT, and open-source models via the `ug configure --agents copilot` utility ([November 2026 | Databricks on AWS](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/november)). Additionally, the Databricks Genie plugin connects Grok Bot and Cursor directly to the Genie One Model Context Protocol (MCP) ([November 2026 | Databricks on AWS](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/november)).
* **BI File Imports:** Genie Code now permits the automated import of Power BI and Tableau files, translating them into AI/BI dashboards and metric views ([Databricks Release Notes - November 2026 Latest Updates - Releasebot](https://releasebot.io/updates/databricks)). This feature will roll out by default on December 15, 2026, for workspaces utilizing compliance security profiles ([Databricks Release Notes - November 2026 Latest Updates - Releasebot](https://releasebot.io/updates/databricks)).

### Data Engineering and Lakeflow Automation
Data pipeline and integration features have matured significantly to support multi-cloud enterprise demands.
* **Lakeflow Designer and Pipelines:** Lakeflow Designer outputs now support writing results directly to Google Drive or SharePoint via the Output operator, with file creation limits capped at 2.75 MiB per run ([November 2026 | Databricks on AWS](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/november)). Furthermore, parameterizing Lakeflow pipeline SQL source code with key-value pairs became generally available in mid-October, allowing a single pipeline to run dynamically across multiple catalogs, schemas, or tables ([October 2026 - Azure Databricks | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/databricks/release-notes/product/2026/october)).
* **Lakebase and Storage Updates:** Lakebase has been updated to incorporate PostgreSQL minor versions 18.7, 17.12, and 16.16 to address upstream security patches ([Databricks Release Notes - November 2026 Latest Updates - Releasebot](https://releasebot.io/updates/databricks)). Structured Streaming upserts to Lakebase now support customizable merge strategies (such as retaining first/last values or ignoring nulls) under Databricks Runtime 19 and above ([November 2026 | Databricks on AWS](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/november)).
* **Connectors:** A managed PayPal connector entered Beta in Lakeflow Connect, allowing automated, incremental ingestion of transaction, invoice, and billing data using OAuth client credentials ([October 2026 - Azure Databricks | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/databricks/release-notes/product/2026/october)).

### Summary of Recent Platform Updates

| Feature / Tool | Release Status / Window | Core Functionality & Strategic Impact |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Genie One Desktop App** | Generally Available (macOS) | Native desktop application for querying and operationalizing data workflows ([Databricks Release Notes - November 2026 Latest Updates - Releasebot](https://releasebot.io/updates/databricks)). |
| **Unity Gateway Copilot Integration** | November 2026 | Connects GitHub Copilot CLI and VS Code to advanced LLMs under admin-defined parameters ([November 2026 | Databricks on AWS](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/november)). |
| **Genie Code BI Imports** | Preview (Default Dec 15, 2026) | Converts legacy Power BI and Tableau files into native AI/BI dashboards and metric views ([Databricks Release Notes - November 2026 Latest Updates - Releasebot](https://releasebot.io/updates/databricks)). |
| **Lakeflow Parameterization** | Generally Available | Enables dynamic multi-environment execution using key-value pair parameters ([October 2026 - Azure Databricks | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/databricks/release-notes/product/2026/october)). |
| **PayPal Connector (Lakeflow)** | Beta | Facilitates incremental ingestion of financial and billing data ([October 2026 - Azure Databricks | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/databricks/release-notes/product/2026/october)). |

## Talking Points
* **Leveraging Enterprise Context with Genie:** Emphasize that Databricks' core strategic advantage lies in reducing the friction between scattered data and actionable business decisions by using governed context layers (such as Genie Ontology) rather than generic chat interfaces ([DAIS 2026: The Databricks Announcements I Think Cl... - Databricks Community - 159914](https://community.databricks.com/t5/community-articles/dais-2026-the-databricks-announcements-i-think-clients-should/td-p/159914)).
* **Developer Productivity via Unity Gateway:** Highlight the operational benefits of integrating coding assistants like GitHub Copilot, Cursor, and Grok Bot securely into the Unity Gateway ecosystem, establishing structured governance over AI-generated code and queries ([November 2026 | Databricks on AWS](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/november)).
